title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 185 (Consideration not necessary)

content.overview: Section 185 provides that no consideration is necessary to create an agency.
content.glance: No consideration is necessary to create an agency.
content.study: No consideration is necessary to create an agency. Current-law framing: agency may be created gratuitously.

sections.heading: Core rule
sections.body: No consideration is necessary to create an agency.

examples.title: Gratuitous agency
examples.body: A person may act as agent without any consideration under Section 185.

hypotheticals.question: Is consideration required to create a valid agency?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 185 expressly provides that no consideration is necessary to create an agency.

enhancement.definition: No consideration is necessary to create an agency.

essentialIngredients: Absence of any requirement of consideration for creation of agency
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 185 provides that no consideration is necessary to create an agency. An agency relationship may therefore be created gratuitously.
examples: A person may agree to act as agent without payment or other consideration.
distinctions: Unlike many contracts, agency does not require consideration for its creation.
problemApplication: Identify that the question concerns consideration for agency.
Conclude that none is necessary under Section 185.
